source.title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems

accepted.question_text: Let G be either the square, hexagonal, or triangular grid in the plane, positioned so that 0 is a vertex of G. For each n, consider the uniform measure on all n-step self-avoiding walks in G that start at 0 and stay in the upper half-plane, and let γ denote a sample from the weak limit of these measures as n tends to infinity. Prove that the scaling limit of the rescaled path sγ exists as s decreases to 0, and that this limit is SLE_{8/3}. The convergence may be understood either in the Hausdorff topology on closed subsets of the Riemann sphere or in the stronger weakly-uniform topology on capacity-parameterized curves described earlier in the paper.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 ([60]). Let γ be a sample from the n → ∞ limit of the uniform measure on n-step self avoiding paths in the upper half plane described above. Prove that the limit as s ց 0 of the law of s γ exists and that it is SLE8/3.

accepted.question_text: Let D be a bounded planar domain whose boundary is a simple path in the triangular lattice, and let ∂+ and ∂− be complementary boundary arcs whose common endpoints are midpoints of edges. Consider the uniform measure on functions h taking odd integer values on the vertices in D, satisfying h = 1 on ∂+, h = -1 on ∂−, and |h(v) - h(u)| in {0, 2} whenever v and u are neighboring vertices. Extend h to D by affine interpolation on each triangle, and let γ be the unique connected component of h^{-1}(0) joining the two boundary endpoints shared by ∂+ and ∂−. Is it true that the interface γ converges to SLE_4, and does the law of h converge to the Gaussian free field in the same sense discussed for related height models?

evidence.quote: Consider the uniform measure on functions h taking odd integer values on vertices in D such that h = 1 on ∂+, h = −1 on ∂−, and |h(v) − h(u)| ∈ {0, 2} for neighbors v, u. ... There is then a unique connected path γ that is the connected component of h−1(0) that contains the two endpoints of each of the two arcs ∂±.
Problem 2.2. Is it true that the path γ tends to SLE4? Does the law of h converge to the Gaussian free field?

accepted.question_text: In the same domain-and-boundary-arc setup as the previous height-model problem, fix λ in (0, 1/2]. Consider the uniform measure on real-valued functions h on the vertices of D such that h = λ on ∂+, h = -λ on ∂−, and |h(v) - h(u)| ≤ 1 for every edge [v, u]. Is there a value of λ for which the corresponding interface converges to SLE_4, and does the law of h converge, in some natural sense, to the Gaussian free field?

evidence.quote: Now suppose that (D, ∂+, ∂−) is as above. Let λ ∈ (0, 1/2] be some constant and consider the uniform measure on functions h taking real values on vertices in D such that h = λ on ∂+, h = −λ on ∂− and |h(v) − h(u)| ≤ 1 for every edge [v, u].
Problem 2.3. Is it true that for some value of λ the corresponding interface converges to SLE4? Does the law of h converge in some sense to the Gaussian free field?

accepted.question_text: Take the Gaussian free field in the domain-and-boundary-arc setup above, project it onto the subspace spanned by Dirichlet Laplacian eigenfunctions with eigenvalues in [-r, r], and then add the harmonic function whose boundary values are +λ on ∂+ and -λ on ∂−. When λ is chosen appropriately, does the resulting zero-level interface converge to SLE_4 as r tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4 ([81]). If we project the Gaussian free field onto the subspace spanned by the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet Laplacian with eigenvalues in [−r, r] and add the harmonic function with boundary values ±λ on ∂±, does the corresponding interface converge to SLE4 as r → ∞ when λ is chosen appropriately?

accepted.question_text: Consider the Ising model on vertices of a triangular-lattice approximation of a domain D with boundary split into complementary arcs ∂+ and ∂−, with spins fixed to +1 on ∂+ and -1 on ∂−. A spin configuration h has probability proportional to exp(-2βk), where k is the number of edges [v, u] across which h(v) and h(u) differ. Prove that at the critical inverse temperature β = β_c the interface converges to SLE_3, and that for every β in (0, β_c) the interface converges to SLE_6.

evidence.quote: Now consider a function h that take the values ±1 on vertices in D such that h is 1 on ∂+ and −1 on ∂−. On the collection of all such functions we put a probability measure such that the probability for a given h is proportional to e−2βk, where β is a parameter and k is the number of edges [v, u] such that h(v) 6= h(u).
Problem 2.5. Prove that when β = βc, the interface converges to SLE3 and when β ∈ (0, βc) to SLE6.

accepted.question_text: Consider the Fortuin-Kasteleyn random-cluster model on Z^2 with parameter q in (0, 4), and with p chosen to be sqrt(q)/(1 + sqrt(q)), the self-dual value. With appropriate boundary conditions defining an interface, prove that the interface converges to SLE_κ, where κ = 4π / arccos(-sqrt(q)/2).

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6 ([76]). Prove that when q ∈ (0, 4) and p = √q/(1+√q), the interface of the FK model on Z2 with appropriate boundary conditions converges to SLEκ, where κ = 4 π/ cos−1(−√q/2).

accepted.question_text: Consider the O(n) loop model on the hexagonal lattice with two distinguished boundary vertices of degree 1, so that configurations consist of one simple boundary-to-boundary path together with disjoint loops. Let x_c(n) = (2 + sqrt(2 - n))^{-1/2}. Prove that when n is in [0, 2] and x = x_c(n), the scaling limit of the distinguished path is chordal SLE_κ for κ in [8/3, 4], and when x > x_c(n), the scaling limit is chordal SLE_κ for κ in [4, 8], with n = -2 cos(4π/κ).

evidence.quote: Now we specialize to the hexagonal lattice. Set xc(n) := (2 + √(2 − n))−1/2, which is the conjectured critical parameter [72].

Problem 2.7 ([36]). Prove that when n ∈ [0, 2] and x = xc(n) [respectively, x > xc(n)] the scaling limit of the path containing the two special boundary vertices is chordal SLEκ, where κ ∈ [8/3, 4] [respectively, κ ∈ [4, 8]] and n = −2 cos(4 π/κ).

accepted.question_text: Fix n ≥ 1 and let T be a uniformly random tree contained in a planar grid G that contains the origin and has exactly n vertices. Determine the growth rate of the expected diameter of T. After rescaling graph distances so that the expected or median diameter is 1, determine whether the law of T has a limit as n tends to infinity, and if so describe the geometric and topological properties of that limit.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. What is the growth rate of the expected diameter of such a tree? If we rescale the tree so that the expected (or median) diameter is 1, is there a limit for the law of the tree as n → ∞? What are its geometric and topological properties? Can the limit be determined?

accepted.question_text: For the model of uniformly random lattice trees with n vertices containing the origin, produce an efficient algorithm that samples such trees approximately uniformly, or prove that no such efficient approximate-uniform sampler exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9. Produce an efficient algorithm which samples lattice trees approximately uniformly, or prove that such an algorithm does not exist.

accepted.question_text: In critical site percolation on the triangular lattice in the upper half-plane with mesh ε, choose a parameter p(ε) so that the probability of a left-to-right white crossing of a fixed 1×1 square equals a prescribed value q in (0, 1), with q ≠ 1/2. The resulting interface is an unbounded path starting at 0. Determine the scaling limit of this interface as ε tends to 0 under this near-critical tuning of p(ε).

evidence.quote: Suppose that in Figure 3 with small mesh ǫ > 0 we choose p(ǫ) so that the probability to have a left to right crossing of white hexagons in some fixed 1 × 1 square in the upper half plane is q at percolation parameter p = p(ǫ).
Problem 2.10 (Lincoln Chayes (personal communication)). What is the scaling limit of the interface as ǫ ց 0 and p = p(ǫ) if q 6= 1/2 is fixed?

accepted.question_text: Prove Smirnov's conformal-invariance theorem for critical bond percolation on the square lattice Z^2.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.11. Prove Smirnov’s theorem for critical bond percolation on Z2.

accepted.question_text: Prove an analogue of Smirnov's theorem for Voronoi percolation, turning the known conformal-invariance information for this model into a full theorem of the same type as in critical site percolation on the triangular lattice.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.12. Prove Smirnov’s theorem for Voronoi percolation.

accepted.question_text: Prove an analogue of Smirnov's theorem for boolean continuum percolation in the plane.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.13. Prove Smirnov’s theorem for boolean percolation.

accepted.question_text: For critical planar percolation, improve coarse asymptotic estimates such as R^{-5/48+o(1)} for the probability that the cluster of the origin has diameter at least R and R^{-5/4+o(1)} for the probability that a given site is pivotal for a crossing event, as well as analogous estimates for related events. In particular, obtain formulas that are sharp up to multiplicative constants, and ideally more precise asymptotics.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. Improve the estimates R−5/48+o(1) and R−5/4+o(1) mentioned above (as well as other similar estimates) to more precise formulas. It would be especially nice to obtain estimates that are sharp up to multiplicative constants.

accepted.question_text: Obtain effective quantitative estimates for the speed at which discrete models that are already known to converge to SLE approach their scaling limits.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Obtain reasonable estimates for the speed of convergence of the discrete processes which are known to converge to SLE.

accepted.question_text: In critical percolation on the square [0, R]^2, condition on the event that there is a left-right crossing. Determine the exponent α for which the expected length of the shortest such crossing grows like R^{α+o(1)} as R tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Calculate the number α such that on the event that there is a left-right crossing in critical percolation in the square [0, R]2, the expected length of the shortest crossing is Rα+o(1).

accepted.question_text: Let μ_n be the uniform measure on equivalence classes of triangulations of the sphere with n vertices, where two triangulations are identified if a homeomorphism of the sphere carries one to the other. Regard a sample X_n as a compact metric space with graph distances rescaled by n^{-1/4}, and let μ_n^* be its law in the space of compact metric spaces with the Gromov-Hausdorff metric. Show that the weak limit of μ_n^* exists as n tends to infinity, and determine the properties of the limiting random compact metric space.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Show that the weak limit limn→∞ µ∗n with respect to the Gromov-Hausdorff metric exists. Determine the properties of the limit.

accepted.question_text: Let f_ℓ be the Boolean crossing function for critical site percolation in an approximately ℓ×ℓ square of the triangular lattice, and let ˜μ_{f_ℓ} denote the induced probability measure on Fourier-Walsh levels |S|. Is it true that ˜μ_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) tends to 1 as ℓ tends to infinity whenever α_1 < 3/4 < α_2? More generally, determine the asymptotic behavior of ˜μ_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) for arbitrary 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1. Is it true that limℓ→∞ ˜µfℓ([ℓα1, ℓα2]) = 1 if α1 < 3/4 < α2? Determine the asymptotic behavior of ˜µfℓ([ℓα1, ℓα2]) as ℓ → ∞ for arbitrary 0 ≤ α1 < α2 ≤ 2.

accepted.question_text: For critical percolation crossing events, identify the Fourier index set S with a random subset of the unit square by rescaling the lattice mesh while keeping the square size fixed. Prove that the corresponding probability measures on closed subsets of the square converge weakly to a limiting measure μ, and determine geometric properties of a μ-typical set S, such as whether it is supported on singletons, on the entire square, or on Cantor-type sets.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 (Gil Kalai, personal communication). Prove that the limiting measure µ exists and determine properties of samples from µ.

accepted.question_text: For dynamical critical site percolation on the triangular lattice with mesh ε, choose the flip rate λ = λ(ε) so that the correlation between a left-right crossing of a fixed square at times 0 and 1 equals 1/2. Prove that the scaling limit of this time-dependent percolation process exists as ε tends to 0. Also prove that crossing-event correlations between times t_1 < t_2 decay to 0 as t_2 - t_1 tends to infinity, and that changes in crossing events become unlikely as t_2 - t_1 tends to 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.3. Prove that the scaling limit of dynamical critical percolation exists. Prove that correlations between crossing events at different times t1 < t2 decay to zero as t2 − t1 → ∞ and that a change in a crossing event becomes unlikely if t2 − t1 → 0.

accepted.question_text: Take a random walk on a fine-mesh lattice approximation of the unit disk, stopped when it first hits the boundary, together with its loop erasure. In any subsequential scaling limit, the pair should converge to a coupling of Brownian motion and SLE_2. In that limiting coupling, is the SLE_2 path determined by the Brownian motion path?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. In this coupling, is the SLE2 determined by the Brownian motion?

accepted.question_text: Consider the uniform spanning tree on a fine square-grid approximation of a torus. The dual graph formed from the dual edges perpendicular to primal edges not in the tree contains exactly three edge-simple closed paths, each of which is non-null-homotopic. Determine the joint distribution of the three homotopy classes represented by these closed dual paths, as a function of the geometry of the torus.

evidence.quote: There is a random graph dual to the tree, which consists of the dual edges perpendicular to primal edges not in the tree. It is not hard to see that this random dual of the tree contains precisely three edge-simple closed paths (i.e., no repeating edges), and that these paths are not null-homotopic.
Problem 6.2. Determine the distribution of the triple of homotopy classes containing these three closed paths.

accepted.question_text: For an SLE_κ path, define a Hausdorff-type measure on the path that is σ-finite and is almost surely finite on compact subsets of the plane. In particular, construct a natural measure that captures the intrinsic size of the SLE trace.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Define a Hausdorff measure on the SLE path which is σ-finite.

accepted.question_text: Fix κ < 8 and let γ be the SLE_κ path in the upper half-plane. Find necessary conditions, sufficient conditions, or both, on a deterministic compact set K ⊂ H that guarantee a positive probability that γ intersects K. The special case K ⊂ R is of particular interest.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2. Fix κ < 8. Find necessary or sufficient conditions on a deterministic compact set K ⊂ H to satisfy P(K ∩ γ 6= ∅) > 0, where γ is the SLEκ path. The case K ⊂ R is of particular interest.

accepted.question_text: Let γ be chordal SLE_κ with κ ≤ 8. Prove that, up to reparametrization, the image of γ under inversion in the unit circle, z ↦ 1/z̄, has the same law as γ itself. Equivalently, establish reversibility of chordal SLE_κ under this inversion symmetry in the stated range of κ.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.3. Let γ be the chordal SLEκ path, where κ ≤ 8. Prove that up to reparametrization, the image of γ under inversion in the unit circle (that is, the map z 7→ 1/z¯) has the same law as γ itself.
